introduction--docs.content: import { Meta } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks"; # Carbon Components Ember An Ember implementation of IBM's [Carbon Design System](https://carbondesignsystem.com), kept in parity with [`@carbon/react`](https://react.carbondesignsystem.com). ## Installation ```sh pnpm add carbon-components-ember @carbon/styles ``` ### Compatibility - **Ember:** tested against `ember-source` 7 (the current release), and in CI against the beta and alpha channels too. - **Apps:** it's a v2 addon for strict-mode templates (`.gts` and `.gjs`). Loose-mode `.hbs` templates can't resolve its components by name (``). Embroider/Vite apps work as-is; classic ember-cli apps need `ember-auto-import` 2 and `ember-template-imports`. Load Carbon's styles and the addon's own stylesheet once, in your app's entry point: ```ts import "@carbon/styles/css/styles.css"; import "carbon-components-ember/styles.css"; ``` ## Usage Import components straight into your `.gts` templates: ```gts import { Button } from "carbon-components-ember/components"; ``` Services are namespaced under `carbon.`: ```ts import { service } from "@ember/service"; class MyComponent { @service("carbon.notifications") notifications; saved = () => this.notifications.success({ title: "Saved" }); } ``` The notifications service shows its toasts in a `ToastNotificationList`, rendered once in the application template. Every component page in the sidebar is generated from the component's own Glint signature: the args table, blocks and element come straight from the source, and each story doubles as a browser test. Stories follow Carbon React's: the same pages, names and variants, and each story file lists any React story it can't match yet. ## Use with AI agents The package ships an [agent skill](https://agentskills.io) for coding agents: how to use the components, how Carbon's React-based docs and designs carry over to Ember, and these docs for the version your app has installed. With pnpm 12.11 or later, approve it once with `pnpm approve carbon-components-ember` and name your agents' skills folders in `skills.dirs`. The [README](https://github.com/IBM/carbon-components-ember#use-with-ai-agents) covers the requirements, and the steps for TanStack Intent, npm and Yarn. [`carbon-components-ember-mcp`](https://github.com/IBM/carbon-components-ember/tree/main/carbon-components-ember-mcp#readme) serves the same docs over MCP, and gives agents the skill's instructions when they connect. Install it in your app, and add it from your app's directory, for example in Claude Code: ```sh pnpm add -D carbon-components-ember-mcp claude mcp add carbon-components-ember -- npx --no carbon-components-ember-mcp ```
